input:
This executive summary provides an overview of delivery performance at a contract packaging firm that operates 2 plants and generates revenue of $76 million per year. The analysis is based on a comprehensive review of order records covering a period of 12 months and encompassing no fewer than 11368 orders, providing a robust evidence base for the findings that follow.

Over the last two quarters, on-time delivery stood at 88%, falling short of the target of 95%. Overtime cost reached $1.7 million last year, an increase of 19% compared with the year before, while the order backlog currently stands at 3.7 weeks, compared with just 1.6 weeks a year ago, highlighting a deteriorating operational picture. A closer look at the data reveals that Plant 2 accounts for 60% of all late orders, suggesting that the delivery challenge is concentrated rather than spread evenly across the business.

A scheduling system for all plants has been quoted at $275k, while Plant 2 alone would cost $137k. The figure for the first stage is $137k, the quoted cost for Plant 2 alone. That $137k tests the programme where 60% of late orders arise. An internal estimate, rather than a vendor figure, suggests that the overtime reduction at Plant 2 could be in the region of 15-20% in the first year. Against this backdrop, the recommendation under consideration is to install the system at Plant 2 first and to hold the other plants until the results from Plant 2 have been reported. The operations director owns the scheduling programme and would oversee the rollout.
